Circumscribe

/SUR-kuhm-skryb/ - the stress falls on SUR · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Circumscribe means to restrict or limit within narrow bounds.

The scholarship's fine print circumscribed her choices: three approved majors, one campus, and no semesters abroad.

Worked Example

For years the tiny apartment circumscribed the painter's ambitions — nothing wider than the hallway could leave the building — so she mastered small panels until the co-op offered her its garage.

Circumscribe literally means to draw a line around: whatever sits inside the circle may move, but never past it. Where limit is flat and factual, circumscribe emphasizes the closed boundary — powers, options, or a whole life held within narrow bounds.

How Circumscribe Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

restrict

restrict: the everyday word for holding within limits

confine

confine: keeps something inside a space or set of bounds

Antonyms

widen

widen: to push the bounds outward instead of drawing them in

unbind

unbind: to undo the restraints altogether

How Strong Is It? — curb → circumscribe → imprison

curb vs. circumscribe

curb vs. circumscribe: Curb is milder than circumscribe: a curb checks one impulse or expense, while circumscribing draws a boundary around the whole field of action.

imprison vs. circumscribe

imprison vs. circumscribe: Imprison goes further than circumscribe: a circumscribed life is hemmed in but still moving; a prisoner's walls end the question.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — circum-

Prefix — circum-: around

Root — scribe

Root — scribe: to write, to draw a line (Latin scribere)

Put it together

Put it together: Circum- (around) + scribe (to write, to draw) = to draw a line around. What is circumscribed sits inside a drawn circle and cannot pass it — the picture behind 'to restrict within narrow bounds.' The same scribere runs through this unit: you will meet it again in proscribe.

Use the root in a new word: inscribe

Use the root in a new word: inscribe: The winners' names are inscribed on a brass plate inside the trophy's lid.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Circumscribe suits writing about powers, rights, and lives held within drawn bounds — charters, constitutions, biographies. For physical or casual squeezes, use constrain (this unit); for the vivid image of chains dragging at someone, use fetter (this unit).
